subject: Re: HelioCloud — Singapore capacity qualification and sizing scan
messages:
From: Susan Lam <susan.lam@heliocloud.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@heliocloud.com
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 23:12:00 +08:00
Subject: Singapore capacity qualification — initial profile

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. HelioCloud is heads-down on a Singapore pilot that starts mid-July. Before we get the procurement cycle moving, we need a short technical qualification to understand what dedicated footprint we'd need if we go dedicated (reserved GPU pools) vs. burst to Hosted. High-level asks: 

- Baseline concurrent sessions: 120 sustained (spiky to 400 during daily batch windows)
- Typical sequence lengths: L=512 for chat, L=2k for periodic batch reranking
- Model target: Llama-3-70B equivalent (we're open to quantized variants)
- Latency SLO: 95th < 220ms for interactive chat (Singapore edge)
- Data residency: logs retained in-region; SOC2 evidence request will follow

I've attached our current capacity profile export (helio_capacity_profile.xlsx). Can your team do a quick sizing scan and outline the minimal Dedicated pool we'd need in SG with a runway plan (3/6/12 months)? Also include any fallback or burst patterns we should budget for.

We have a commercial sponsor lined up but procurement expects a ballpark by EOW.

Best,
Susan
Head of Platform, HelioCloud
[attachment: helio_capacity_profile.xlsx]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lam <susan.lam@heliocloud.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Singapore capacity qualification — initial profile

Susan — thanks for the detail and the file. We're happy to run a short sizing qualification and will deliver a three-tier proposal (Conservative / Production / Aggressive) with recommended node counts, expected per-token cost deltas vs Hosted, and SLO mappings for the three time horizons you called out.

Quick clarifying Qs so our sizing assumptions match your workload:
- Are the 120 concurrent sessions steady-state or a rolling daily average?
- The 2k batch windows — are those scheduled (daily batch 02:00 local) or ad-hoc spikes?
- Any current preference on quantization (FP16, 4-bit q4, or int8)? If not, we will recommend the best tradeoff for cost vs quality.

I'll loop in Karthik and Ben to scope the infra-side assumptions. Expect our first pass by EOD Tue (your timezone).

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | logan.wright@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: HelioCloud — Singapore capacity qualification and sizing scan

Team — forwarding Helio's profile. They need a 3/6/12 month sizing scan and a minimal Dedicated pool recommendation for Singapore (edge). Key constraints: 120 steady-ish concurrent, spikes to 400, latency SLO 95th <220ms, models ~70B family, batch windows up to 2k seq.

Assumptions I think we should validate:
- Target model runtime: 70B quantized (q4/8) to hit cost targets; fallback to 70B FP16 only for highest quality routes.
- Node type candidate: A100-80GB or H100-80GB depending on q-profile; we should give costed alternatives.
- Burst strategy: Dedicated reserved for sustained baseline (120 sessions), plus Routed Burst to Hosted (or cross-region failover) for peak 400. Need playbook for fallbacks to keep SLOs.

Deliverables: 1) 3-tier node count and SKU mix 2) per-token cost delta vs Hosted 3) suggested autoscale triggers and burst lanes 4) short SOC2 evidence checklist for procurement

Olga — can you run a quick capacity model (attached CSV from Helio) and propose node mixes? Karthik — can you list SKU+cost estimates and confirm whether fractional node options apply for this deal? Ben — flag any commercial constraints for a pilot (credits/seat).

Thanks,
Logan

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: HelioCloud — Singapore capacity qualification and sizing scan

Thanks Logan — ran a quick model using Helio's profile. Notes below and attached a short worksheet (RDW_calc_helio_sg.csv).

High-level recommendations (short form):
- Conservative (pilot / POC): 4x H100-80GB nodes (quantized q4) — supports ~110-140 sustained concurrent with 2k batch offload to scheduled job runners. Latency 95th ~180-210ms in-region.
- Production (initial commercial): 10x H100-80GB nodes + 2x standby A100 (cross-region failover) — supports ~350 sustained if we rely on bursting routes for peak 400; expected 95th ~150-210ms depending on mix.
- Aggressive (reserved for growth): 16x H100 nodes + 4x A100 standby — sustained 500+ with redundancy and headroom for model upgrades.

Quantization note: q4 (mixed quant) gives best cost/latency balance. Recommend offering Helio a trial on q4 with a gating eval; hold FP16 routes for <1% of requests (high-fidelity).

Operational notes:
- Autoscale policy: scale-up at moving-average concurrency >85% baseline, scale-down after 12m cool-down.
- Burst lanes: primary burst to Hosted with sticky routing for in-flight sessions; fallback to EU region if Singapore sub-60s provisioning fails (need cross-region latency test).
- SOC2 and evidence: we can provide logs, KMS configuration, and per-route access logs. Procurement will ask for retention policies — standard 90/180/365 options documented.

Attachments: RDW_calc_helio_sg.csv, sizing_notes.md

Olga
Senior Infra Planner, Redwood Inference
[attachment: RDW_calc_helio_sg.csv]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lam <susan.lam@heliocloud.com>, ops@heliocloud.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HelioCloud — Singapore capacity qualification and sizing scan

Susan — attaching our 3-tier proposal and an initial SOW outline (RDW_SOW_draft_v1.2.pdf). Summary below: 

- Pilot (Conservative): 4x H100-80GB, quantized runtime, 3-month pilot price with reserved baseline and Hosted burst lanes. Estimated monthly committed cost: USD 67k (approx).
- Initial Commercial (Production): 10x H100-80GB + 2x standby A100, 12-month commitment recommendation with 20% burst buffer. Estimated monthly committed cost: USD 152k (approx).
- Growth (Aggressive): 16x H100 + 4x A100 standby, 12–24 month reserved profile. Estimated monthly committed cost: USD 238k (approx).

Action items we propose:
1) Helio confirms whether 120 concurrent is steady or average (Susan).
2) Helio agrees to a short quantization QA run (q4) — Redwood provides eval.
3) If Helio wants an FP16 lane, we will scope separate SOW pricing (higher cost).
4) Redwood will share SOC2 evidence bundle and retention options in <48h.

Attachments: RDW_SOW_draft_v1.2.pdf, helio_capacity_profile.xlsx (original)

If that sounds good I can route a commercial ballpark to your procurement contact and spin up a trial agreement.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: RDW_SOW_draft_v1.2.pdf]
